Definition: to break off or loose (in a favorable or unfavorable sense), i.e. desist (from grief) or invade (with destruction)
BiblicalUsage: Balag means to break off, to let go, to desist, and it cuts both ways. Amos says God strengthens the spoiled against the strong, breaking off destruction against them, while Job begs to break off his grief for a moment, to leave off complaining and take comfort before his days run out.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe there is mercy in this word, because God knows when to stop the blow and when to let a weary man rest. Job asked for a little breathing room, and I hold that God hears that prayer even when the answer is slower than we want.
